mouth.definition: The opening in the face used for eating and speaking.
mouth.sentence: The dentist asked me to open my mouth.

company.definition: A group of people gathered together.
company.origin: French from a Latin formation meaning people who share bread.
company.sentence: The pleasant company made the long trip enjoyable.

lovely.origin: English love with the adjective ending -ly.
lovely.sentence: The garden looked lovely in the spring sunshine.

path.definition: A route or track used for walking.
path.sentence: A narrow path led through the woods.

source.definition: The place or thing from which something comes.
source.origin: French from Latin surgere, to rise.
source.sentence: The spring was the source of the village's water.

market.definition: A place where people buy and sell goods.
market.sentence: We bought fresh vegetables at the market.

year.sentence: We visit our cousins once each year.

result.definition: Something that happens because of an action or event.
result.origin: Related to Latin resultare, originally to spring back.
result.sentence: The broken window was the result of a stray ball.

truck.definition: A large motor vehicle for carrying goods.
truck.origin: Originally a word for a small wheel or wheeled vehicle.
truck.sentence: The truck delivered boxes to the store.

whale.definition: A large sea mammal that breathes air.
whale.sentence: The whale rose to the surface to breathe.

down.definition: Toward a lower place or position.
down.origin: From Old English of dune, meaning from the hill.
down.sentence: The ball rolled down the slope.

body.definition: The physical form of a person or animal.
body.sentence: Exercise helps keep your body strong.

most.origin: Old English maest, a superlative related to more.
most.sentence: She collected the most shells of anyone on the beach.

total.definition: The whole amount after parts are added together.
total.origin: French from Medieval Latin totalis, related to totus, whole.
total.sentence: The total of three and four is seven.

hurt.sentence: The sharp stone could hurt your foot.

shell.definition: A hard outer covering that protects an animal.
shell.sentence: The turtle pulled its head into its shell.

easy.definition: Not difficult to do or understand.
easy.sentence: The first puzzle was easy to solve.

tallest.definition: Having the greatest height in a group.
tallest.origin: Superlative of tall, with the English ending -est.
tallest.sentence: The tallest tree towered above the others.

truth.origin: Old English treowth, related to faithfulness.
truth.sentence: She told the truth about the broken vase.

seventy.definition: The number equal to seven tens.
seventy.origin: Old English seofontig, combining seven and tens.
seventy.sentence: The library bought seventy new books.

house.sentence: Our house has a blue front door.

hopped.origin: Past tense of hop, from Old English hoppian.
hopped.sentence: The frog hopped onto the lily pad.

flock.definition: A group of birds or sheep.
flock.sentence: A flock of geese crossed the sky.

yarn.definition: A long thread used for knitting or weaving.
yarn.sentence: She knitted a scarf from soft yarn.

trouble.origin: French from a Latin verb related to disturbing.
trouble.sentence: The flat tire caused trouble on our trip.

sound.definition: Something heard through vibrations reaching the ears.
sound.sentence: The sound of the bell called us inside.

remember.definition: To bring something back into the mind.
remember.origin: French remembrer, related to Latin memor, mindful.
remember.sentence: I remember the first time I rode a bike.

grumpily.definition: In an irritable or bad-tempered way.
grumpily.origin: English grumpy with the adverb ending -ly.
grumpily.sentence: He grumpily complained about getting up early.

shine.definition: To give out or reflect bright light.
shine.sentence: The stars shine brightly on clear nights.

illness.definition: A disease or state of being unwell.
illness.origin: English ill with the noun ending -ness.
illness.sentence: The illness kept her in bed for two days.

entire.origin: French entier, from Latin integer, whole.
entire.sentence: We ate the entire loaf of bread.

relax.definition: To become calm or less tense.
relax.sentence: I like to relax with a book after school.

peer.definition: To look closely or with difficulty.
peer.origin: Recorded in Middle English; its earlier origin is uncertain.
peer.sentence: We had to peer through the fog to see the boat.

sprout.definition: To begin growing from a seed or plant.
sprout.sentence: The seeds will sprout after we water them.

shivering.definition: Shaking slightly because of cold or fear.
shivering.origin: From shiver, recorded in Middle English.
shivering.sentence: The shivering puppy curled up in a warm blanket.

dirt.definition: Loose earth or an unwanted dirty substance.
dirt.origin: Middle English drit, from Old Norse.
dirt.sentence: Mud and dirt covered his boots.

knit.definition: To make cloth by looping yarn together with needles.
knit.origin: Old English cnyttan, related to knot.
knit.sentence: She learned to knit a warm hat.

cloak.definition: A loose outer garment that hangs from the shoulders.
cloak.origin: French cloque, originally a bell, named for its shape.
cloak.sentence: The traveler wrapped a woolen cloak around his shoulders.

rod.definition: A long, thin, straight bar or stick.
rod.sentence: He used a metal rod to support the plant.

hiking.definition: Walking a long distance, especially in the countryside.
hiking.origin: From hike, an English word whose earlier origin is uncertain.
hiking.sentence: We went hiking on the mountain trail.

carve.definition: To cut a shape or design from a material.
carve.sentence: He used a small tool to carve a wooden bird.

crack.definition: A narrow break or split in something.
crack.origin: Related to an Old English word for a sharp breaking noise.
crack.sentence: A crack appeared in the old flowerpot.

parade.definition: A public procession for a celebration or display.
parade.origin: French, ultimately from a word for preparing or arranging.
parade.sentence: The band marched at the front of the parade.

friend.definition: A person you like and trust.
friend.origin: Old English freond, related to loving.
friend.sentence: My friend helped me finish the puzzle.

dangle.origin: Probably of Scandinavian origin; the exact history is uncertain.
dangle.sentence: The keys dangle from a hook beside the door.

pearls.definition: Smooth, shiny objects formed inside certain shellfish.
pearls.origin: Plural of pearl, borrowed through French.
pearls.sentence: Her necklace was made of white pearls.

breeze.sentence: A cool breeze moved the curtains.

shadows.definition: Dark areas formed where something blocks the light.
shadows.origin: Plural of shadow, from Old English sceadu.
shadows.sentence: The trees cast long shadows across the path.

sharp.definition: Having an edge or point that can cut or pierce.
sharp.sentence: Be careful with the sharp scissors.

whistle.definition: To make a high sound by blowing air through the lips.
whistle.origin: Old English hwistlian, imitating the sound.
whistle.sentence: He can whistle a cheerful tune.

ran.origin: Past tense of run, from Old English forms including rinnan.
ran.sentence: The dog ran across the yard.

apple.definition: A round fruit with firm flesh and a thin skin.
apple.sentence: She packed a red apple in her lunch.

earth.sentence: The gardener dug into the soft earth.

wrong.sentence: I erased the wrong answer and tried again.

crunch.definition: To crush or chew with a crisp breaking sound.
crunch.origin: An English word formed in imitation of a sound.
crunch.sentence: We could hear the horse crunch a carrot.

beasts.definition: Animals, especially large or wild ones.
beasts.origin: Plural of beast, from French and Latin bestia.
beasts.sentence: The story described strange beasts in the forest.

chips.definition: Thin slices of food cooked until crisp.
chips.origin: Plural of chip, from an Old English word for cutting.
chips.sentence: We shared a bowl of potato chips.

voice.definition: The sound made by someone speaking or singing.
voice.sentence: Her clear voice carried across the room.

steps.definition: Movements made by lifting and placing the feet.
steps.origin: Plural of step, from Old English stepe.
steps.sentence: We took careful steps across the icy pavement.

foolish.origin: English fool with the adjective ending -ish.
foolish.sentence: It was foolish to leave the bike unlocked.

narrow.sentence: Only one person could fit through the narrow doorway.

heart.definition: The organ that pumps blood around the body.
heart.sentence: Exercise makes your heart beat faster.

ampulla.definition: A small flask or rounded vessel with a narrow neck.
ampulla.origin: Borrowed from a Latin word for a small flask.
ampulla.sentence: The archaeologist found a clay ampulla beside the ancient coins.

ototoxic.definition: Harmful to the ear, especially to hearing or balance.
ototoxic.origin: Oto-, from Greek for ear, combined with toxic.
ototoxic.sentence: The researcher tested whether the chemical was ototoxic.

decisively.definition: In a firm way that settles a question or outcome.
decisively.origin: Decisive with the adverb ending -ly, ultimately related to Latin decidere, to decide.
decisively.sentence: She acted decisively and stopped the leak.

neurological.definition: Relating to the brain, spinal cord, and nerves.
neurological.origin: From neurology, using Greek neuron, nerve, and an element meaning study.
neurological.sentence: The doctor performed a neurological examination to check his reflexes.

chickadee.definition: A small North American bird with a distinctive call and often a dark cap.
chickadee.origin: An imitation of the bird's call.
chickadee.sentence: A chickadee perched on the snowy feeder.

sensilla.definition: Small sensory structures on the bodies of insects and other invertebrates.
sensilla.origin: Plural of sensillum, a New Latin diminutive related to Latin sensus, sense.
sensilla.sentence: The insect's sensilla detected movement near its antennae.

conspicuous.origin: Latin conspicuus, related to conspicere, to look at.
conspicuous.sentence: Her bright orange hat was conspicuous in the crowd.

prosciutto.definition: Italian ham that is salted and dried rather than cooked.
prosciutto.origin: Italian, ultimately from a Latin formation meaning dried thoroughly.
prosciutto.sentence: The chef placed thin slices of prosciutto on the platter.

Delaware.definition: A United States state on the Atlantic coast, with Dover as its capital.
Delaware.origin: Named after the river and bay, whose name honors the English governor Lord De La Warr.
Delaware.sentence: We visited Delaware during our trip along the Atlantic coast.

credenza.definition: A low cabinet or sideboard used for storage.
credenza.origin: Italian, related to a word for belief or trust, from Latin credere.
credenza.sentence: The dishes were stored in a wooden credenza.

auditory.origin: Latin audire, meaning to hear, through an adjective formation.
auditory.sentence: The auditory test measured how well she could hear faint sounds.

mysticetes.definition: Baleen whales, which strain food from water using plates in their mouths.
mysticetes.origin: From the New Latin zoological name Mysticeti; its older Greek derivation has been debated.
mysticetes.sentence: The mysticetes filtered tiny animals from the seawater.

irrelevant.definition: Not connected with the matter being considered.
irrelevant.origin: Ir-, meaning not, combined with relevant.
irrelevant.sentence: The judge excluded the irrelevant detail from the discussion.

apologetic.definition: Expressing regret for a mistake or offense.
apologetic.origin: Related to Greek apologia, a speech in defense.
apologetic.sentence: His apologetic note explained why he had missed the meeting.

sputum.definition: Material coughed up from the lungs or air passages.
sputum.origin: From Latin for something spat out, derived from spuere, to spit.
sputum.sentence: The laboratory examined the patient's sputum sample.

psychological.definition: Relating to the mind, feelings, or behavior.
psychological.origin: From psychology, using Greek psyche, mind or soul, and an element meaning study.
psychological.sentence: The story explored the psychological effects of isolation.

curriculum.definition: The subjects and courses taught by a school or program.
curriculum.origin: From Latin for a running course, related to currere, to run.
curriculum.sentence: The new curriculum includes science, art, and music.

pulmonary.sentence: The medical diagram showed the pulmonary blood vessels.

assemblage.definition: A collection of things or people brought together.
assemblage.origin: French, formed from assembler, to bring together.
assemblage.sentence: The display contained an assemblage of shells from many beaches.

endothermy.definition: The ability to generate body heat internally and regulate body temperature.
endothermy.origin: Endo-, meaning within, with a Greek element meaning heat.
endothermy.sentence: The lesson explained how endothermy helps birds stay warm.

trichobothria.definition: Long sensory hairs that detect air movement and vibrations in many arachnids and some insects.
trichobothria.origin: Plural of trichobothrium, using Greek elements for hair and a small pit.
trichobothria.sentence: The spider's trichobothria sensed the moving air nearby.

echolocation.definition: Finding objects by sending out sounds and listening to their echoes.
echolocation.sentence: The bat used echolocation to find insects in the dark.

arugula.definition: A leafy plant with a peppery taste, eaten in salads.
arugula.origin: From an Italian dialect form related to Latin eruca.
arugula.sentence: She added fresh arugula to the salad.

Amharic.definition: A Semitic language spoken widely in Ethiopia.
Amharic.origin: Amhara, the name of a people and region, with the ending -ic.
Amharic.sentence: The guide greeted the visitors in Amharic.

subscription.definition: An arrangement to receive a service or publication regularly.
subscription.origin: Latin subscriptio, related to subscribere, to write underneath or sign.
subscription.sentence: Our subscription delivers a science magazine every month.

legation.definition: A diplomatic mission headed by a minister, or its official premises.
legation.origin: Latin legatio, an embassy, related to legare, to send as an envoy.
legation.sentence: The ambassador met the visiting officials at the legation.

vibrometer.origin: Vibro-, relating to vibration, with -meter, a measuring instrument.
vibrometer.sentence: The engineer used a vibrometer to examine the shaking bridge.

foliage.definition: The leaves of a plant or plants together.
foliage.origin: French feuillage, ultimately from Latin folium, leaf.
foliage.sentence: The thick foliage shaded the forest floor.

mortar.definition: A mixture used to hold bricks or stones together.
mortar.origin: French from Latin mortarium, a vessel for pounding materials.
mortar.sentence: The builder spread mortar between the bricks.

inaugurate.definition: To formally begin something or install someone in office.
inaugurate.origin: Latin inaugurare, associated with taking omens before an official act.
inaugurate.sentence: The town will inaugurate its new museum on Saturday.

doberman.definition: A dog of a German breed with a muscular body and short coat.
doberman.origin: Named for German breeder Karl Friedrich Louis Dobermann.
doberman.sentence: The doberman stood alert beside the gate.

generosity.definition: Willingness to give or share freely.
generosity.origin: Latin generositas, related to generosus, noble.
generosity.sentence: Her generosity supplied books for the entire class.

finesse.definition: Skillful, delicate handling of a task or situation.
finesse.origin: From French, derived from fin, meaning fine.
finesse.sentence: The dancer moved with remarkable finesse.

forsythia.definition: A shrub that produces bright yellow flowers in early spring.
forsythia.origin: A New Latin plant name honoring botanist William Forsyth.
forsythia.sentence: The forsythia bloomed before its leaves appeared.

sentinels.definition: People or animals that stand guard and watch for danger.
sentinels.origin: Plural of sentinel, through French from Italian sentinella.
sentinels.sentence: The sentinels watched the gate throughout the night.

torrential.definition: Falling in a very heavy, rushing flow.
torrential.origin: From torrent, ultimately Latin torrens, rushing or burning.
torrential.sentence: Torrential rain flooded the narrow streets.

leprosy.definition: A chronic bacterial disease that can affect the skin and peripheral nerves.
leprosy.origin: Through French from Greek lepra, a scaly condition.
leprosy.sentence: The history exhibit described advances in treating leprosy.

a cappella.origin: Italian phrase meaning in the manner of the chapel.
a cappella.sentence: The choir sang a cappella in the quiet hall.

panoramic.definition: Providing a wide view of an area.
panoramic.origin: From panorama, using Greek elements meaning all and view.
panoramic.sentence: The hilltop offered a panoramic view of the valley.

authority.definition: The power or right to make decisions and enforce rules.
authority.origin: French from Latin auctoritas, influence or power.
authority.sentence: The principal has authority to set the school rules.

innocuous.definition: Harmless and unlikely to cause offense or injury.
innocuous.origin: Latin innocuus, combining not with nocere, to harm.
innocuous.sentence: The innocuous little beetle did not damage the plants.

enigmatic.origin: From enigma, through Latin from Greek ainigma, a riddle.
enigmatic.sentence: Her enigmatic smile gave no clue to the answer.

gauntlets.definition: Protective gloves, especially ones covering part of the forearm.
gauntlets.origin: French gantelet, a diminutive related to gant, glove.
gauntlets.sentence: The knight pulled on heavy gauntlets before the contest.

solenodon.definition: A nocturnal Caribbean mammal with a long snout and venomous saliva.
solenodon.origin: A New Latin genus name using Greek elements for channel and tooth.
solenodon.sentence: The solenodon searched the forest floor for insects at night.

tenuous.definition: Weak, slight, or not firmly established.
tenuous.sentence: The argument depended on a tenuous connection between the events.

influenza.definition: A contagious viral illness that commonly causes fever, aches, and coughing.
influenza.origin: From Italian for influence, reflecting an old belief in the influence of the stars.
influenza.sentence: Several students stayed home after catching influenza.

chitinous.definition: Made of or containing the tough substance found in insect outer coverings.
chitinous.origin: Chitin, from Greek chiton, a tunic, with the ending -ous.
chitinous.sentence: The beetle's chitinous shell protected its body.

embankment.definition: A raised bank of earth or stone used for support or protection.
embankment.origin: From embank with the noun ending -ment.
embankment.sentence: Grass covered the steep embankment beside the railway.

trenchant.origin: French, related to trancher, to cut.
trenchant.sentence: Her trenchant criticism exposed the weakness in the plan.

despondent.origin: Latin despondere, to give up or lose hope.
despondent.sentence: He felt despondent after several failed attempts.

juniper.definition: An evergreen tree or shrub that often bears small berry-like cones.
juniper.sentence: A juniper grew on the rocky hillside.

propeller.definition: A rotating device whose blades move a boat or aircraft through water or air.
propeller.origin: From propel, Latin propellere, to drive forward.
propeller.sentence: The airplane's propeller began to spin.

eureka.definition: An exclamation used when a discovery or solution is found.
eureka.origin: Greek heureka, meaning I have found it.
eureka.sentence: Eureka, she cried when the puzzle finally made sense.

butane.definition: A flammable gas used as fuel.
butane.origin: From butyl with the chemical ending -ane; butyl is related to Latin butyrum, butter.
butane.sentence: The camping stove used butane as its fuel.

thermotaxis.definition: Movement by an organism in response to temperature.
thermotaxis.origin: Greek-derived thermo-, heat, combined with taxis, arrangement or directed movement.
thermotaxis.sentence: The experiment measured thermotaxis as the organisms moved toward warmth.

approximation.definition: An estimate or value that is close to the exact one.
approximation.origin: From approximate, ultimately Latin approximare, to come near.
approximation.sentence: We used an approximation of the distance to plan the trip.

mewling.definition: Crying softly in a weak or complaining way.
mewling.origin: From mewl, a word imitating a small crying sound.
mewling.sentence: The mewling kitten searched for its mother.

spes phthisica.definition: An unrealistic hope of recovery associated historically with advanced tuberculosis.
spes phthisica.origin: Latin phrase combining spes, hope, with phthisica, relating to consumption or tuberculosis.
spes phthisica.sentence: The historical medical text described the patient's optimism as spes phthisica.

Presbyterian.definition: Relating to a Christian tradition governed by elected elders.
Presbyterian.origin: From presbyter, through Latin from Greek presbyteros, elder.
Presbyterian.sentence: The family attended a Presbyterian church.

unrelenting.definition: Not easing, weakening, or giving way.
unrelenting.origin: Un-, meaning not, with relenting, yielding or becoming less harsh.
unrelenting.sentence: The unrelenting heat dried the fields.

Addis Ababa.origin: An Amharic place name meaning new flower.
Addis Ababa.sentence: The travelers arrived in Addis Ababa before continuing their journey.

seminal.definition: Highly influential in the development of later ideas or work.
seminal.sentence: Her seminal paper inspired a new field of research.

procession.definition: A group moving together in an orderly line.
procession.origin: Latin processio, related to procedere, to go forward.
procession.sentence: The procession moved slowly through the town square.

Tripoli.definition: The capital city of Libya, on the Mediterranean coast.
Tripoli.origin: Through Arabic and earlier forms from Greek Tripolis, meaning three cities.
Tripoli.sentence: The ship docked near Tripoli on the Mediterranean coast.

dominion.definition: Control or rule over a territory.
dominion.sentence: The king claimed dominion over the neighboring islands.

asymmetric.definition: Having sides or parts that do not match in shape or arrangement.
asymmetric.sentence: The artist chose an asymmetric design with a single large curve.

persistent.definition: Continuing firmly despite difficulty or opposition.
persistent.origin: From Latin persistere, to stand firm.
persistent.sentence: The persistent student kept practicing until she mastered the skill.

annelids.definition: Segmented worms, including earthworms and leeches.
annelids.origin: From a zoological name based on Latin annellus, a little ring.
annelids.sentence: The biologist examined annelids collected from the soil.

Cappadocia.definition: A historical region of central Anatolia, in present-day Turkey.
Cappadocia.origin: Through Greek from an Old Persian place name; its ultimate meaning is uncertain.
Cappadocia.sentence: The travelers photographed the unusual rock formations of Cappadocia.

alabaster.definition: A soft, pale mineral used for carvings and ornaments.
alabaster.origin: Through French and Latin from Greek alabastros.
alabaster.sentence: The sculptor carved a small bowl from alabaster.

reluctance.definition: Unwillingness or hesitation to do something.
reluctance.origin: From reluctant, related to Latin reluctari, to struggle against.
reluctance.sentence: Her reluctance to enter the cave faded when she saw the lights.

blithely.definition: In a cheerful, carefree, or unconcerned way.
blithely.origin: Blithe, from Old English blithe, with -ly.
blithely.sentence: He blithely sang as he walked down the path.

lemmings.definition: Small rodents found mainly in northern regions.
lemmings.sentence: The lemmings sheltered beneath the snow.

burnished.origin: From burnish, through French brunir, to polish or make brown.
burnished.sentence: The burnished brass handle gleamed in the sunlight.

palazzo.definition: A large, grand Italian house or palace.
palazzo.sentence: The old palazzo overlooked the canal.

phantasmal.definition: Ghostly or resembling an unreal vision.
phantasmal.origin: From phantasm, through Latin from Greek phantasma, an appearance.
phantasmal.sentence: A phantasmal figure seemed to drift through the fog.

arsonists.definition: People who deliberately set unlawful fires.
arsonists.origin: From arson, through French from Latin ardere, to burn, with -ist and plural -s.
arsonists.sentence: Investigators searched for the arsonists who had burned the warehouse.

acolyte.definition: A person who assists in a religious service.
acolyte.origin: Through Latin from Greek akolouthos, follower.
acolyte.sentence: The acolyte carried a candle to the altar.

hemisphere.definition: One half of a sphere or globe.
hemisphere.origin: Greek hemi-, half, with sphaira, sphere.
hemisphere.sentence: The equator separates each hemisphere from the other.

hypothesis.definition: A proposed explanation that can be tested.
hypothesis.origin: From Greek for a supposition or something placed underneath.
hypothesis.sentence: The scientist tested her hypothesis with a controlled experiment.

consulate.definition: The office or building of a government's representative in a foreign city.
consulate.origin: From consul, a Latin official title.
consulate.sentence: The traveler asked the consulate for help replacing a passport.

éclair.definition: An oblong pastry filled with cream and usually topped with icing.
éclair.origin: French word meaning a flash of lightning.
éclair.sentence: She chose a chocolate éclair from the bakery case.

self-sufficient.definition: Able to meet one's needs without outside help.
self-sufficient.origin: English self combined with sufficient, from Latin sufficere, to be enough.
self-sufficient.sentence: The self-sufficient farm produced its own food and electricity.

modish.definition: Fashionable or following the latest style.
modish.origin: Mode, from French for fashion, with the ending -ish.
modish.sentence: Her modish jacket drew compliments at the party.

salicylic acid.definition: A chemical compound used in some medicines and skin-care products.
salicylic acid.origin: Named in relation to salicin, from Latin salix, willow, where related substances occur.
salicylic acid.sentence: The label listed salicylic acid among the product's ingredients.

odorant.definition: A substance that gives off a smell.
odorant.origin: From Latin odor, smell, through an adjective meaning giving off an odor.
odorant.sentence: An odorant was added to the gas to make leaks noticeable.

quiche.definition: An open pastry tart with a savory egg-and-cream filling.
quiche.origin: French, borrowed from a German dialect word related to cake.
quiche.sentence: The bakery served a vegetable quiche for lunch.

frequency.definition: The number of repeating cycles or events in a given time.
frequency.origin: Latin frequentia, related to frequens, frequent or crowded.
frequency.sentence: The scientist measured the frequency of the sound waves.

cataract.definition: A clouding of the eye's lens that can reduce vision.
cataract.origin: Through Latin from Greek katarraktes, a waterfall or something falling down.
cataract.sentence: The eye examination revealed a cataract in the older patient's lens.

Bildungsroman.definition: A novel about a person's growth and development from youth.
Bildungsroman.origin: German Bildung, formation or education, with Roman, novel.
Bildungsroman.sentence: The class read a Bildungsroman about a young artist discovering her identity.

cul-de-sac.definition: A street closed at one end.
cul-de-sac.origin: French phrase literally meaning bottom of a bag.
cul-de-sac.sentence: The children rode their bicycles around the quiet cul-de-sac.

diffidence.definition: A lack of confidence that makes a person shy or hesitant.
diffidence.origin: Latin diffidentia, mistrust or lack of confidence.
diffidence.sentence: Her diffidence made speaking before the audience difficult.

arachnid.definition: An animal such as a spider or scorpion, usually with eight legs.
arachnid.origin: Greek arachne, spider, through a zoological formation.
arachnid.sentence: The scorpion is an arachnid rather than an insect.

alleviate.definition: To make pain or difficulty less severe.
alleviate.sentence: Rest helped alleviate the soreness in her legs.

thrummed.definition: Made a steady, low humming or vibrating sound.
thrummed.origin: Past tense of thrum, an imitation of a sound.
thrummed.sentence: The engine thrummed beneath the deck.

saxophone.definition: A wind instrument with a single reed and a curved metal body.
saxophone.origin: Named for its inventor Adolphe Sax, with Greek phone, sound.
saxophone.sentence: The musician played a mellow solo on the saxophone.

prospective.definition: Expected or likely to happen or become something in the future.
prospective.sentence: The guide showed the campus to prospective students.

comprehensible.origin: Latin comprehensibilis, related to comprehendere, to grasp.
comprehensible.sentence: The teacher gave a clear and comprehensible explanation.

generator.definition: A machine that converts mechanical energy into electrical energy.
generator.origin: From Latin for one who produces, related to generare.
generator.sentence: The generator supplied electricity during the power outage.

mayonnaise.definition: A thick sauce made by mixing oil with egg and an acid such as vinegar.
mayonnaise.origin: Borrowed from French; the earlier origin of the name is disputed.
mayonnaise.sentence: He spread mayonnaise on the sandwich.

conflagration.origin: Latin conflagratio, related to conflagrare, to burn up.
conflagration.sentence: The conflagration destroyed several buildings before firefighters contained it.

undulating.definition: Moving in a smooth, wave-like pattern.
undulating.origin: From undulate, related to Latin unda, wave.
undulating.sentence: The flag was undulating in the gentle breeze.

diplomatically.definition: With tact and skill in handling people or disagreements.
diplomatically.origin: Diplomatic with -ally, ultimately related to Greek diploma, a folded document.
diplomatically.sentence: She diplomatically suggested a compromise that pleased both sides.

embodiment.definition: A concrete example or expression of an idea or quality.
embodiment.origin: From embody, combining em- with body, and -ment.
embodiment.sentence: The volunteer was an embodiment of kindness.

crocheted.definition: Made fabric by looping thread or yarn with a hooked needle.
crocheted.origin: Past tense of crochet, from French for a small hook.
crocheted.sentence: She crocheted a blanket for the new baby.

affinities.origin: Plural of affinity, from Latin affinitas, relationship.
affinities.sentence: The two languages have affinities in their vocabulary.

cuisine.definition: A style or tradition of cooking.
cuisine.origin: From French for kitchen, ultimately from Latin coquina.
cuisine.sentence: The restaurant specializes in Italian cuisine.

bioluminescence.definition: Light produced by chemical reactions inside living organisms.
bioluminescence.origin: Bio-, life, with luminescence, related to Latin lumen, light.
bioluminescence.sentence: The firefly's glow is an example of bioluminescence.

canter.definition: A horse's smooth, three-beat gait faster than a trot.
canter.origin: Shortened from Canterbury gallop, associated with pilgrims riding toward Canterbury.
canter.sentence: The horse moved across the field at a canter.

porpoises.definition: Small toothed sea mammals related to dolphins, usually with rounded snouts.
porpoises.origin: Through French from Latin elements meaning pig and fish.
porpoises.sentence: The porpoises surfaced beside the boat.

brazier.definition: A container that holds burning coals for heating or cooking.
brazier.sentence: The travelers warmed their hands beside the brazier.

quizzically.definition: With a puzzled or questioning expression.
quizzically.origin: Quizzical with the adverb ending -ly, related to quiz.
quizzically.sentence: He looked quizzically at the upside-down sign.

censers.definition: Containers in which incense is burned.
censers.origin: Plural of censer, through French from Latin incensarium.
censers.sentence: Fragrant smoke rose from the swinging censers.

Pennsylvania.definition: A United States state with Harrisburg as its capital.
Pennsylvania.origin: Named for William Penn's father, with Latin silva, forest, in a formation meaning Penn's woodland.
Pennsylvania.sentence: Our class visited Pennsylvania to learn about early American history.

lactobacillus.definition: A rod-shaped bacterium that produces lactic acid from sugars.
lactobacillus.origin: New Latin combining elements for milk and a small rod.
lactobacillus.sentence: The laboratory identified a lactobacillus in the culture.

frankincense.definition: An aromatic tree resin burned as incense.
frankincense.origin: French elements meaning high-quality or pure incense.
frankincense.sentence: The room smelled of burning frankincense.

stomatopods.definition: Marine crustaceans known as mantis shrimps, with powerful grasping or striking limbs.
stomatopods.origin: From New Latin Stomatopoda, using Greek elements for mouth and foot.
stomatopods.sentence: The stomatopods hid in burrows among the reef rocks.

kerosene.definition: A liquid fuel made from petroleum.
kerosene.origin: Coined from Greek keros, wax, with a chemical ending.

sauntered.origin: Past tense of saunter; its earlier origin is uncertain.
sauntered.sentence: They sauntered through the park after lunch.

preconception.definition: An opinion formed before enough information is known.
preconception.origin: Pre-, before, with conception, from Latin concipere, to form or take in.
preconception.sentence: Her visit challenged her preconception about life in the city.

pathologically.definition: In a way related to disease or an unhealthy condition.
pathologically.origin: From pathological, using Greek pathos, suffering, and an element for study, with -ly.
pathologically.sentence: The tissue was pathologically altered by the disease.

lapels.definition: The folded-back edges on the front of a coat or jacket.
lapels.origin: Plural of lapel, a diminutive of lap, a flap or fold.
lapels.sentence: He pinned a flower to one of his jacket's lapels.

imperial.definition: Relating to an empire or emperor.
imperial.origin: Latin imperialis, related to imperium, command or empire.
imperial.sentence: The imperial palace contained a vast ceremonial hall.

vibrissae.definition: Stiff sensory hairs, such as the whiskers of a cat.
vibrissae.origin: Plural of Latin vibrissa, related to vibrare, to vibrate.
vibrissae.sentence: The cat's vibrissae helped it sense the narrow opening.

eponymous.origin: Greek-derived elements for upon and name, through eponym.
eponymous.sentence: The eponymous heroine gives the novel its title.

cerulean.origin: Latin caeruleus, blue or dark blue.
cerulean.sentence: The artist painted the sea a cerulean shade.

yakuza.definition: Members of organized criminal groups in Japan.
yakuza.origin: Japanese, traditionally linked to a losing card combination of eight, nine, and three.
yakuza.sentence: The documentary examined the history of the yakuza in Japan.

bogong moth.definition: An Australian moth known for seasonal migration to alpine areas.
bogong moth.origin: The first element comes from an Aboriginal Australian word associated with the brown moth.
bogong moth.sentence: A bogong moth rested in the cool mountain cave.

electrolytes.definition: Substances that form electrically charged particles when dissolved and can conduct electricity.
electrolytes.origin: Electro-, electricity, with an element from Greek lytos, capable of being dissolved.
electrolytes.sentence: The science lesson explained how dissolved electrolytes conduct electricity.

wallowing.definition: Rolling or lying in mud, water, or a similar substance.
wallowing.origin: From wallow, related to Old English wealwian, to roll.
wallowing.sentence: The buffalo were wallowing in the muddy pool.

perpendicular.definition: Meeting a line or surface at a right angle.
perpendicular.origin: Latin perpendicularis, relating to a plumb line.
perpendicular.sentence: The two lines were perpendicular and formed a right angle.

increments.definition: Small amounts by which something increases.
increments.origin: Plural of increment, from Latin incrementum, growth.
increments.sentence: We raised the height in small increments until the model balanced.

appetizing.definition: Making food seem appealing to eat.
appetizing.origin: From appetite, ultimately Latin appetitus, desire, with an English ending.
appetizing.sentence: An appetizing smell drifted from the kitchen.

inanimate.origin: Latin inanimatus, combining not with animatus, alive or animated.
inanimate.sentence: A stone is an inanimate object.

Sierra Leone.definition: A West African country on the Atlantic coast, with Freetown as its capital.
Sierra Leone.origin: An adapted form of Portuguese Serra Leoa, meaning lion mountains.
Sierra Leone.sentence: The travelers arrived in Sierra Leone during the rainy season.

calibrate.definition: To check or adjust an instrument so that its measurements are accurate.
calibrate.origin: From caliber, through French calibre, with the verb ending -ate.
calibrate.sentence: The technician will calibrate the scale before weighing the samples.

Eritrea.definition: A country on the Red Sea coast of northeastern Africa, with Asmara as its capital.
Eritrea.origin: From an Italian geographical name based on a Greek name associated with the Red Sea.
Eritrea.sentence: The ship sailed along the coast of Eritrea.

phenomenon.origin: Greek phainomenon, something appearing or seen.
phenomenon.sentence: The rainbow was a beautiful natural phenomenon.

newt.definition: A small amphibian with a long tail, related to salamanders.
newt.origin: An alteration of an older English phrase an ewt, with the n transferred to the noun.
newt.sentence: A newt swam between the pond plants.

euphemism.definition: A mild expression used in place of one considered harsh or unpleasant.
euphemism.origin: Greek euphemismos, from elements for good and speaking.
euphemism.sentence: Passed away is a euphemism for died.

Aphrodite.definition: The Greek goddess of love and beauty.
Aphrodite.origin: A Greek divine name whose ultimate origin is uncertain; a traditional story connects it with aphros, foam.
Aphrodite.sentence: The ancient statue depicted Aphrodite standing beside a shell.

unconscious.definition: Not awake or aware of one's surroundings.
unconscious.origin: Un-, meaning not, with conscious, from Latin conscius, knowing.
unconscious.sentence: The unconscious patient did not respond until later.

Krio.definition: An English-based creole language spoken in Sierra Leone.
Krio.origin: Through the language's own name from Portuguese crioulo, creole.
Krio.sentence: The guide translated the announcement into Krio.

Gloucester.definition: A city in southwestern England beside the River Severn.
Gloucester.origin: An English place name based on the Roman name Glevum with an Old English element for a fortified town.
Gloucester.sentence: We visited the cathedral in Gloucester during our trip.

irascibility.definition: A tendency to become angry easily.
irascibility.origin: From irascible, related to Latin irasci, to grow angry.
irascibility.sentence: His irascibility made minor delays seem like major problems.

glycerin.definition: A sweet, colorless, thick liquid used in many products.
glycerin.origin: French glycerine, based on Greek glykeros, sweet.
glycerin.sentence: The soap maker measured the glycerin into a clean container.

reassurance.definition: Words or actions that help someone feel less worried.
reassurance.origin: Re-, again, with assurance, related to assure.
reassurance.sentence: Her calm reassurance helped the nervous child feel safe.
